title: Choose the visual world for the CRM
question: Re-rolled on your steer: light, restrained, minimal. The roll assigned The Drawing Sheet.

options.label: The Drawing Sheet
options.lineage: engineering drawing sheets and drafting standards
options.thesis: Every lead is a sheet on the board: a title block, a revision history, and one red mark where something changed.
options.viewport: One continuous sheet under a pale grid: a title block carrying today's counts, then lead rows ruled like a schedule table, with revision red used only where something is late or has changed.
options.risk: Reads cold and clinical if the type is set meanly, and tips into blueprint cliche the moment the grid gets loud.

raised.raise: One continuous field owns the whole frame, rather than a scatter of floating cards.
A single module governs inbox, board, agenda and detail alike, so the system stays recognisable in every view.
Selection inverts the row itself instead of adding a coloured badge beside it.
A keyboard-first command line creates and advances leads, and states print as text rather than as chrome.
Every earlier step stays visible on the sheet: history is part of the record, not hidden behind a tab.
Hierarchy is carried by type weight and scale, never by a box where a hairline will do.

options.label: The Carbon Bill Book
options.thesis: Each lead tears off as a numbered slip, and the carbon under-copy stays bound in the book forever.
options.viewport: A bound stack of numbered slips, the current one raised, its carbon copy showing through beneath.
options.risk: It is the obvious pick for a billing product, and perforation detail can turn into skeuomorphic decoration fast.

options.label: One-bit desktop
options.thesis: Black and white pixels only, dithered greys, marching ants around every selection.
options.viewport: Overlapping windows on a dithered desktop, selections walking with ants.
options.case: Declined: it honours your no-dark, no-vibrant steer, but overlapping windows and dither fight a dense responsive lead list, and it identifies with computing nostalgia rather than your working world.
options.kept: State by inversion rather than added chrome.
options.risk: Dither destroys legibility exactly where the data gets dense.

options.label: Alphabet storm
options.thesis: Letters condense into words, break into weather, and carve the landscape.
options.viewport: Type behaving as matter across an open white field.
options.case: Declined: light and restrained as asked, but typography-as-physics cannot carry a sortable list of two hundred leads, and nothing about it identifies with running a studio.
options.kept: Type carrying structure in place of boxes.
options.risk: Spectacle where the task needs a table.

options.label: Yeye pop sleeve
options.thesis: One flat saturated ground per release, a portrait cropped square, four titles in a corner.
options.viewport: A tangerine field with a cropped face and a tidy corner block.
options.case: Declined: ruled out by your steer on saturation alone, and its closed set of four tracks is the opposite of an open, growing lead list.
options.kept: One flat field owning the entire frame.
options.risk: Saturated grounds are exactly what you asked to avoid.

options.label: Modular identity blocks
options.thesis: Photography and hard vector bars snapping together under one loud grammar of coloured blocks.
options.viewport: Saturated bars stacked over a staged photograph, fragments locking to a module.
options.case: Declined: the loud grammar is precisely what your steer excludes, and colour bars compete with the data they are meant to organise.
options.kept: A module system that survives however far the parts are thrown.
options.risk: Colour doing decoration's job while the table does the work.

options.label: Phosphor terminal
options.thesis: A living transcript on curved glass, cursor breathing, afterimages trailing the scroll.
options.viewport: One continuous scrolling transcript in a fixed 80-column field.
options.case: Declined: dark ground is ruled out by your steer, and a transcript is the wrong shape for scanning a pipeline at a glance.
options.kept: Typed input as a first-class control, with states printed rather than chromed.
options.risk: A conversation log where you need a sorted board.

options.label: Orizuru fold sequence
options.thesis: One uncut vermilion sheet passing through numbered folds into a standing bird.
options.viewport: A numbered crease sequence beside the folded form, every earlier crease still readable.
options.case: Declined: a vermilion ground is out on your steer, and a fixed thirty-two-step sequence misdescribes leads, which skip stages and go backwards.
options.kept: Every earlier step remaining visible in the finished object.
options.risk: A fixed sequence imposed on an unfixed process.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every CRM ships, executed impeccably: left icon rail, white ground, pastel kanban.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement you already expect, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from HubSpot or Pipedrive, by design.
